abstractText: Abstract A multigene phylogenetic assessment of European and North American species in Inocybe sect. Petiginosae based on ITS, LSU and RPB2 rDNA sequence data was undertaken to enable a systematic revision. Specimens collected in northern boreal to arctic-alpine ecosystems were shown to include an unexpected high genetic diversity and revealed several new species. In total, 22 clades were identified as independent species occurring in Europe and North America. Of these clades, 7 represent already described species, namely I. duploparvula , I. egenula , I. glareophila , I. jacobi , I. nigrodisca , I. petiginosa and I. subexilis . The other 15 are described as new species, viz. I. abscondita , I. algida , I. baeocarpa , I. boreonematoloma , I. dryadophila , I. ignota , I. inconspicua , I. melleicolor , I. parilis , I. patellaris , I. paulula , I. peregenula , I. perjacobi , I. pseudotsugae and I. tepidula . In addition, two supported clades including environmental ITS data from the arctic-alpine zones were recovered, suggesting there are more undescribed species to be identified. Lecto-typification of, and an epitype for, I. petiginosa is selected. Inocybe rufoalba and I. fulvella are proposed to be synonyms of I. petiginosa , and I. nematoloma a synonym of I. subexilis . Specimens previously determined to I. nematoloma originating from moist coniferous forests in the northern boreal zone is here described as I. boreonematoloma . We confirm that both I. subexilis and I. nigrodisca occur in Europe. Emended descriptions of described species are provided in addition to the descriptions of new species. A key to the species is provided based on morphology, ecology, host preferences and geographic distribution.

title: A biomimetic 3D printed gradient tri-layered scaffold stimulating osteochondral differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells for mandibular condyle regeneration
abstractText: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to fabricate and assess the physical, mechanical, and in vitro biological properties of 3D printed single-layered scaffolds that simulate cartilage, calcified cartilage, and subchondral bone tissue. As well as a tri-layered osteochondral scaffold with a gradient composition and porosity. Methods Six groups were fabricated using a masked stereolithography-based 3D printer. The cartilage group consisted of polylactic acid (PLA)/ 2% hyaluronic acid (HA) with the smallest pores and percentage porosity. The calcified cartilage group comprised PLA/ 2% HA/10% nano-hydroxyapatite (nHAp). Subchondral bone scaffold was formed of PLA/ 25% nHAp with the largest pore size and % porosity. The three scaffold designs were assembled to create the tri-layered group. There were two control groups. A total of 683 scaffolds were 3D printed. Tensile strength, compressive strength, moduli, and interfacial adhesion strength were evaluated at 24 h and 30 days. The biodegradation % of different scaffolds was assessed after 7, 14, and 28 days. Cell viability was assessed through cell counting, cell adhesion, and H & E staining. Cell differentiation was assessed using fast green/safranin O, alizarin red staining, and immunofluorescence after coculturing with rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem at 7, 14, and 21 days. Data were statistically analyzed at p ≤ 0.05. Results The tensile strengths and moduli of the PLA/2%HA and PLA/25% nHAp scaffolds resembled those of normal cartilage and trabecular bone, respectively. The tri-layered scaffold exhibited strong interfacial adhesion strength and demonstrated 13.68% weight loss after 30 days. The tri-layered scaffold exhibited a stiffness gradient, supporting biological responses consistent with chondrogenic differentiation on the more flexible side of the scaffold and osteogenic differentiation on the stiffer side. It demonstrated evidence of both chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation. Conclusions Incorporation of HA and nHAp, as well as variations in porosity, significantly impacted scaffolds' properties. Clinical relevance These findings suggested the potential of the fabricated scaffolds for medical and maxillofacial regenerative applications, particularly for repairing cartilage, bone, and osteochondral defects.

title: Effect of the excited states on the disappearance of the dynamical interference from the atomic two-photon ionization
abstractText: Abstract By solving the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation accurately, the ionization process of a hydrogen atom under the action of a laser pulse with a frequency of 0.3 a.u. was investigated. The study revealed that with the increase of the driving laser intensity, the ionization probability of the atom declined after rapidly increasing, exhibiting a characteristic of ionization suppression. It is noteworthy that the dynamic interference disappears in a certain range of laser intensities in the ionization suppression zone. Through the analysis of the excited state of the system, it is found that the reason for the disappearance of the dynamic interference phenomenon is that in addition to the direct ionization of electrons from the ground state, there is also the excitation to the excited state first and then ionized from the excited state, the laser intensity for which has not yet reached the ionization suppression requirement in the meantime.

title: Clinical exit strategy in anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular AMD: incidence of recurrence and risk factors for relapse
abstractText: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the recurrence rate of neovascular activity after discontinuation of intravitreal anti–vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and to identify baseline clinical and imaging factors associated with relapse following a clinical exit strategy. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, patients with neovascular AMD who discontinued anti-VEGF therapy due to a clinical decision were identified. Treatment discontinuation was based on the absence of foveal exudation on optical coherence tomography (OCT). Baseline demographic, clinical, and OCT characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was disease recurrence, defined as the need for a new intravitreal anti-VEGF injection during follow-up. Multivariate regression analysis was performed to identify baseline biomarkers associated with relapse. Results Seventy-eight patients (78 eyes) were included (mean age 82.3 ± 5.5 years; 78.2% women). Disease recurrence occurred in 38 patients (48.7%) after a mean of 389.0 ± 247.3 days, with 47.4% of relapses occurring within the first year. Visual acuity significantly worsened between treatment discontinuation and relapse ( p < 0.001). At the time of retreatment, intraretinal fluid, subretinal fluid, and subretinal hyperreflective material were observed in 57.9%, 63.2%, and 55.3% of eyes, respectively. Multivariate regression identified extrafoveal intraretinal fluid and retinal pigment epithelium tear at baseline as biomarkers associated with recurrence. Conclusions Recurrence after anti-VEGF discontinuation is common in neovascular AMD. The presence of extrafoveal intraretinal fluid and retinal pigment epithelium tear at treatment cessation may increase the risk of relapse, highlighting the need for cautious treatment exit strategies and close post-discontinuation monitoring.

VALIDITAS KONSTRUK INSTRUMEN FEAR OF NEGATIVE EVALUATION DENGAN METODE CONFIRMATORY FACTOR ANALYSIS (CFA)
abstractText: ABSTRACT Fear of Negative Evaluation (FNE) is one of the factors associated with social anxiety during adolescence, highlighting the need for an assessment instrument that can accurately measure this construct within the Indonesian cultural context. This study aimed to obtain evidence of content validity and internal structure for the Indonesian version of The Brief Fear of Negative Evaluation Scale II (BFNE-II) among vocational high school students. The adaptation process followed the guidelines of the International Test Commission (2017) through forward translation, translation synthesis, backward translation, and an equivalence assessment conducted by two experts. The study involved 245 students from SMK Negeri 1 Kota Malang, aged 15–19 years, selected using simple random sampling. Content validity was examined using Gregory’s inter-rater agreement index, while the internal structure was assessed through a one-factor Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) using AMOS 23. The results showed a Gregory index of 1.00, while the CFA yielded an adequate model fit with CFI = 0.925, RMSEA = 0.076, and p < 0.001. All 12 items demonstrated positive and significant factor loadings with t > 1.96; therefore, no items were eliminated. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity and internal structure supporting a unidimensional model of the Indonesian BFNE-II among the students studied. Further research should examine reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across more diverse samples. ABSTRAK Fear of Negative Evaluation (FNE) menjadi salah satu aspek yang berkaitan dengan kecemasan sosial pada masa remaja, sehingga diperlukan instrumen yang mampu mengukur konstruk tersebut secara tepat dalam konteks budaya Indonesia. Penelitian ini bertujuan memperoleh bukti validitas isi dan struktur internal The Brief Fear of Negative Evaluation Scale II (BFNE-II) versi bahasa Indonesia pada siswa sekolah menengah kejuruan. Proses adaptasi mengacu pada pedoman International Test Commission (2017) melalui tahapan forward translation, sintesis terjemahan, backward translation, dan penilaian kesepadanan oleh dua ahli. Penelitian melibatkan 245 siswa SMK Negeri 1 Kota Malang berusia 15–19 tahun yang dipilih melalui simple random sampling. Validitas isi dianalisis menggunakan indeks kesepakatan antarahli Gregory, sedangkan struktur internal diuji melalui Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) model satu faktor dengan AMOS 23. Hasil menunjukkan indeks Gregory sebesar 1,00, sedangkan CFA menghasilkan CFI = 0,925, RMSEA = 0,076, dan p < 0,001. Seluruh 12 butir menunjukkan muatan faktor positif dan signifikan dengan nilai t > 1,96 sehingga tidak terdapat butir yang dieliminasi. Temuan ini memberikan bukti awal mengenai kesepadanan isi dan struktur internal BFNE-II versi bahasa Indonesia yang mendukung model satu faktor pada siswa yang diteliti. Pengujian reliabilitas, validitas konvergen dan diskriminan, serta measurement invariance pada karakteristik sampel yang lebih beragam diperlukan pada penelitian berikutnya.

title: Electrochemical Oxidative Dearomatization of Indole with Carboxylic Acid via 1,2-Acyloxy Migration for the Synthesis of C2-Quaternary Indolin-3-ones
abstractText: Abstract Herein, we develop an efficient KBr-promoted electrochemical strategy that enables the oxidative dearomatization of indoles with carboxylic acids via 1,2-acyloxy migration, establishing a mechanistically different method to synthesize structurally diverse C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones using H2O as an oxygen atom source. Mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and isotope-labeling studies, support a C-3 esterification/1,2-acyloxy migration cascade pathway.

title: Gated Memristive Coupling in a Hindmarsh-Rose Neural Network: Nonlinear Dynamics and Hardware Implementation
abstractText: Abstract Inspired by astrocyte-mediated modulation in tripartite synapses, this study proposes a gated memristive coupling mechanism for neural networks. Unlike conventional pairwise coupling scheme with predefined interaction strengths, the proposed framework introduces an independent neuronal state to regulate the evolution of the gated memristive element's state variable, forming a dynamic modulation pathway. Through this mechanism, the coupling strength between two neurons can be continuously adjusted by the activity of a third neuron without directly modifying the intrinsic coupling coefficients. A three-neuron Hindmarsh-Rose network with gated memristive coupling channels is constructed to investigate the resulting nonlinear dynamics. Bifurcation analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-parameter maps reveal that the proposed architecture generates diverse transitions among periodic, multi-periodic, and chaotic firing regimes. Different coupling channels exhibit distinct regulatory characteristics, and their interaction produces complex distributions of dynamical regions in the parameter space. Furthermore, external excitation analysis demonstrates that neuronal inputs provide an additional control pathway by modulating the membrane potential of the gating neuron, thereby indirectly regulating the effective coupling strength. The feasibility of the proposed mechanism is validated through real-time digital signal processor (DSP) implementation, where hardware-generated trajectories agree well with numerical simulations. This work provides a compact and hardware-realizable framework for studying state-dependent neural coupling regulation and offers a potential approach for adaptive neuromorphic systems.

title: Secondary-mass Features Improve Spectral-siren H 0 Constraints
abstractText: Abstract Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) enable independent measurements of the Hubble constant H 0 via the spectral siren method, which critically depends on an accurate model of the source-frame mass distribution. While the primary-mass function has been extensively studied, the impact of the secondary-mass distribution on cosmological inference has been largely overlooked. Here, we perform a joint inference of population and cosmological parameters using 142 confident CBC detections from GWTC-4.0, adopting a new parametric model that flexibly describes features in both the component-mass spectrum and the pairing function, with particular emphasis on the secondary masses. We find H 0 = 71 . 4 − 13.4 + 13.8 km s − 1 Mpc − 1 (68% CL) from spectral sirens alone, and H 0 = 73 . 5 − 7.2 + 9.2 km s − 1 Mpc − 1 when combined with the bright siren GW170817. Compared to the standard LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Collaboration Fullpop-4.0 analysis, these constraints represent improvements of ∼29.8% and ∼22.2% in H 0 uncertainty, respectively. The enhanced precision is driven by previously unmodeled features, including peaks near 18 M ⊙ and 65 M ⊙ as well as mass-dependent pairing transitions at 28 M ⊙ and 52 M ⊙ . Our results demonstrate that the secondary-mass function is also a key ingredient for precision standard-siren cosmology.

title: Implementing and Scaling Artificial Intelligence in Low-Resourced Radiation Oncology: A Systematic Review of Deployments
abstractText: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to address workforce shortages and workflow inefficiencies in radiation oncology, particularly in low-resourced settings where limited specialist capacity constrains access to care. This systematic review evaluated AI deployments in radiation oncology in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and assessed readiness for safe implementation and scale-up. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, six databases were searched from January 2000 through December 2025. Eligible studies were classified using a radiation oncology-specific integration spectrum (Levels 0-4) and evaluated for workflow integration, validation, deployment, and governance characteristics. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Two studies (11.1%) focused on readiness or governance without clinical AI deployment (Level 0), nine (50.0%) reported task-level applications (Level 1), six (33.3%) demonstrated clinician-supervised workflow integration (Level 2), and one (5.6%) reported cross-stage workflow orchestration (Level 3). No study provided sufficient evidence for classification as Level 4 operation. Validation was predominantly retrospective, and continuous performance monitoring was not reported. AI deployment in LMIC radiation oncology remains concentrated at early stages of integration. This pattern reflects not a lack of innovation, but constraints in validation, workflow maturity, infrastructure, and governance. Safe and scalable deployment will require coordinated advances across these domains.

Sentiment Analysis of Indonesian Mobile Banking Reviews on Google Play Store in 2025: A Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms
abstractText: Mobile banking applications generate large volumes of user reviews that can be used to evaluate digital banking service quality. This study analyzes sentiment in Indonesian mobile banking reviews on the Google Play Store in 2025 and compares the performance of Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). A total of 270,977 reviews were collected from five applications, namely BRImo, Livin’ by Mandiri, myBCA, BYOND by BSI, and wondr by BNI. The data were processed through text cleaning, case folding, tokenization, word normalization, stopword removal, and negation retention. Sentiment labels were generated automatically using the InSet Lexicon and validated on 450 stratified review samples. The validation results showed moderate agreement between automatic and manual labels, with an accuracy of 0.6111, macro-F1 score of 0.5384, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.4167. Review texts were represented using TF-IDF with unigram and bigram features, and model performance was evaluated across six stratified data-splitting scenarios using accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro-F1, confusion matrix, and macro ROC-AUC. The results show that RF in Scenario 6 achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 0.9524, macro-F1 score of 0.8498, and macro ROC-AUC of 0.9798. Dominant-term analysis indicates recurring complaints related to login failures, transaction errors, system disruptions, and application updates. This study contributes a cross-application comparison of machine learning algorithms for Indonesian mobile banking sentiment analysis and provides practical insights for improving service reliability. However, the findings should be interpreted within the limitation of automatic lexicon-based labeling, particularly for neutral and context-dependent reviews.

Dislocation-induced artifacts in cyclic voltammetry of battery materials
abstractText: Abstract This review establishes that crystallographic dislocations distort cyclic voltammetry in battery electrode materials, tracing that distortion from its thermodynamic origin through its diagnostic and design consequences across silicon, olivine, spinel, and layered-oxide chemistries. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) is the diagnostic workhorse of battery electrochemistry; experimentalists read peak positions, heights, and shapes as fingerprints of thermodynamic state and reaction kinetics. What the standard interpretation omits is the mechanical condition of the electrode. Crystallographic dislocations inside cathode nanoparticles generate stress fields that couple directly into the electrochemical boundary condition, and the resulting shifts and distortions in the CV response can be misread as purely chemical or kinetic phenomena. This coupling operates across material classes. Voltage hysteresis in silicon anodes, anomalous plateau formation in Mn-substituted olivines, and voltage fade in lithium-rich layered oxides are each a manifestation of the same Butler-Volmer correction in a different host. The mechanistic framework rests on the Larché-Cahn formalism, in which dislocation-induced hydrostatic stress enters the chemical potential of Li intercalation and shifts the equilibrium insertion potential. When the partial molar volume is allowed to vary with lithium content rather than held fixed, the correction produces true distortion of CV peak shape rather than a mere rigid shift. Burgers vector orientation emerges as the controlling variable: one specific orientation raises the effective Li diffusivity extracted from Randles-Ševčík analysis by a factor of 3.3, a mechanical artifact that can be mistaken for genuine transport improvement. CV peak asymmetry, when interpreted through an anisotropic dislocation mechanics inversion, can identify the dominant dislocation character in an electrode without separate structural characterization. Defect engineering, meaning the deliberate introduction of dislocations of a chosen orientation, follows as a practical design strategy, provided the critical density threshold separating beneficial stress relief from crack incubation is not exceeded.

title: Form Measurement of a 300 mm Ellipsoidal Binary Grating Using a Spatio-Temporal Fourier Method
abstractText: Abstract For conventional laser Fizeau phase-shifting interferometry, form measurement of ellipsoidal binary gratings remains challenging because of the discontinuous grating structure with groove depths exceeding half the illumination wavelength. In this study, we propose a spatio-temporal Fourier analysis method that extends conventional laser Fizeau interferometry for full-field form measurement of ellipsoidal binary gratings. By applying a three-dimensional Fourier transform to phase-shifted interferograms, combined with spatial low-pass filtering, the low-spatial-frequency phase is extracted. Moreover, the background intensity is utilized for segmentation masks, enabling independent segmentation and reconstruction of the upper and lower grating surfaces. Simulations show that the residual reconstruction errors remain below 6.5 nm root-mean-square for a groove depth of 2.65 μm. Experimental validation using a 30 mm flat grating agrees well with state-of-the-art point-scanning optical profilometric measurements, where a 300 mm ellipsoidal grating was successfully characterized. The proposed method extends conventional Fizeau interferometry to enable accurate full-field surface form metrology of ellipsoidal binary gratings.

title: Increased CSF PKR activation in Alzheimer’s disease is associated with APOE4 genotype
abstractText: Abstract Objective Protein kinase R (PKR) is a stress-activated kinase implicated in translational control, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. Although increased PKR activation was reported in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), prior studies relied on semi-quantitative methods. This study aimed to quantitatively assess cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) levels of total PKR and phosphorylated PKR (pPKR) in AD patients using the highly sensitive Single Molecule Array (SIMOA) platform and to evaluate their clinical and genetic associations. Methods We developed and applied novel SIMOA assays to measure CSF concentrations of total PKR and pPKR in a cohort of 92 AD patients and neurological controls. Associations with established AD biomarkers, cognitive outcomes, and APOE ε4 (APOE4) genotype were examined. Results CSF pPKR levels and the pPKR/PKR ratio were significantly elevated in AD patients compared with controls. CSF pPKR levels were positively correlated with phosphorylated tau concentrations and with a steeper longitudinal cognitive decline. Notably, among AD patients, higher CSF pPKR levels were associated with APOE4 carrier status, identifying a previously unreported association between this major genetic risk factor and PKR phosphorylation. In contrast, the pPKR/PKR ratio did not differ significantly according to APOE4 status among AD patients. Conclusions Using ultrasensitive SIMOA assays, this study provides independent confirmation of increased CSF PKR phosphorylation in Alzheimer’s disease and identifies an association between APOE4 carrier status and pPKR concentration among patients with AD. These findings support further mechanistic and longitudinal studies to clarify the role of PKR in AD pathophysiology and to evaluate its potential as a biomarker candidate and therapeutic target.

title: Density estimation of lizards (Gallotia galloti) from habitats of Tenerife with different environmental features
abstractText: Abstract Estimating animal population density across different habitats is essential for understanding population dynamics and species responses to environmental variation. We estimated the density of the endemic lizard Gallotia galloti in three habitats on Tenerife: a xeric lowland habitat in the southeast and two high-elevation habitats on the northern slope, one at the upper limit of a pine forest and the other in high-mountain scrubland near Teide National Park. These habitats differ markedly in altitude, climatic conditions, and vegetation structure. We conducted independent line transects at each site during the period of highest lizard activity (April-June) and measured the perpendicular distance from each lizard location to the transect centreline. Using Distance 7.5 software, we found that lizard density was higher at the southern site than at the two northern sites. We compare our data with previous estimates for the same species and other lacertids obtained using the same or different density-estimation methods, and discuss the ecological traits that may be associated with the observed differences in density.

title: Tiga Keluar Satu: Akuntabilitas Sistem Bagi Hasil Petani Kakao di Desa Talabosa
abstractText: Latar belakang: Kabupaten Poso, menerapkan sistem bagi hasil tradisional antara pemilik lahan dan petani penggarap yang dikenal sebagai tiga keluar satu. Sistem ini mencerminkan nilai ekonomi, sosial, budaya, dan akuntabilitas yang berakar pada norma adat lokal (Ada Mpowia), tetapi mekanisme akuntabilitasnya belum didokumentasikan dan dianalisis secara formal. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis praktik akuntabilitas dalam sistem bagi hasil tiga keluar satu pada pertanian kakao di Desa Talabosa. Metode: Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi partisipatif, wawancara mendalam semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi. Informan terdiri atas lima orang yang dipilih secara purposive, yaitu dua pemilik lahan, dua petani penggarap, dan satu tokoh adat. Data dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi. Hasil: Sistem tiga keluar satu membagi hasil panen menjadi dua pertiga untuk pemilik lahan dan sepertiga untuk petani penggarap. Informan memandang pembagian tersebut adil karena pemilik lahan menanggung biaya produksi, sedangkan petani penggarap berkontribusi melalui tenaga dan pengelolaan lahan. Ada Mpowia berfungsi sebagai kerangka akuntabilitas informal, sedangkan digiwu menjadi sanksi adat dan mekanisme kontrol sosial. Kesimpulan: Akuntabilitas diwujudkan melalui keterbukaan pelaporan hasil panen, kepercayaan timbal balik, dan kepatuhan terhadap norma adat. Praktik ini menunjukkan bahwa akuntabilitas bagi hasil pertanian dibangun secara sosial dan kultural, bukan melalui dokumentasi formal.

title: PERAN DUKUNGAN SOSIAL KELUARGA DAN REGULASI EMOSI TERHADAP DISTRES PSIKOLOGIS PADA MASYARAKAT NUSA TENGGARA TIMUR DALAM KETERLIBATAN TRADISI KUMPUL KELUARGA MENJELANG PERKAWINAN DAN PELAKSANAAN ACARA ADAT
abstractText: Involvement in family gathering traditions prior to marriage and indigenous ceremonies in East Nusa Tenggara often imposes financial burdens and emotional strains, yet empirical studies investigating psychological protective factors remain scarce. This study aimed to examine the relationship between family social support and emotion regulation with psychological distress among East Nusa Tenggara communities participating in customary family gatherings. This study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design. The participants comprised 100 individuals aged 18–60 years selected via a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected using the Family Social Support Scale, the Emotion Regulation Scale, and the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10). Data analysis utilized Pearson product-moment correlation supported by IBM SPSS Statistics. The findings revealed a significant negative relationship between family social support and psychological distress (r=-0.500; p<0.001), as well as a significant negative relationship between emotion regulation and psychological distress (r=-0.560; p<0.001). Most participants reported high family social support (59%), high emotion regulation (58%), and low psychological distress (68%). These findings demonstrate that robust family social support and adaptive emotion regulation serve as protective buffers against psychological distress in customary cultural practices. ABSTRAK Keterlibatan dalam tradisi kumpul keluarga menjelang perkawinan dan upacara adat di Nusa Tenggara Timur kerap menimbulkan beban finansial serta tekanan emosional, namun kajian empiris yang meneliti faktor protektif psikologisnya masih sangat terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji hubungan antara dukungan sosial keluarga dan regulasi emosi dengan distres psikologis pada masyarakat Nusa Tenggara Timur yang terlibat dalam tradisi kumpul keluarga adat. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional. Partisipan penelitian berjumlah 100 orang berusia 18–60 tahun yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan Skala Dukungan Sosial Keluarga, Skala Regulasi Emosi, dan Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10). Analisis data menggunakan uji korelasi Pearson product-moment berbantuan program IBM SPSS Statistics. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya hubungan negatif yang signifikan antara dukungan sosial keluarga dan distres psikologis (r=-0,500; p<0,001), serta hubungan negatif yang signifikan antara regulasi emosi dan distres psikologis (r=-0,560; p<0,001). Sebagian besar partisipan memiliki dukungan sosial keluarga tinggi (59%), regulasi emosi tinggi (58%), dan distres psikologis rendah (68%). Temuan ini membuktikan bahwa dukungan sosial keluarga yang kokoh dan regulasi emosi yang adaptif berfungsi sebagai penyangga protektif terhadap distres psikologis dalam pelaksanaan tradisi budaya.

Clinical presentations, complications, and outcomes of benoxinate topical ophthalmic anesthetic abuse: a retrospective cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Topical anesthetic abuse is a concerning ophthalmic morbidity that may lead to irreversible visual loss. The primary goal of this study was to compare the clinical presentations, complications, healing duration and visual acuity changes between topical ophthalmic anesthetic users and non-users after superficial corneal trauma. The secondary goal was to correlate different variables related to the use of topical ophthalmic anesthetics with the final clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective cohort study reviewed files of patients with a positive history of superficial corneal trauma at Alexandria Ophthalmology Hospital Cornea Clinic, Alexandria, Egypt, between January 2021 and January 2026. Patients were divided according to the use of benoxinate eye drops into two groups (benoxinate users and benoxinate non-users). Data extracted included the patient’s job, the cause of the initial injury, the use of topical ophthalmic anesthetic (duration, frequency, and continuation after presentation), clinical picture, complications, healing duration, and visual outcomes. Results A total of 181 eyes in 147 patients was included, 84 eyes in benoxinate users and 97 eyes in benoxinate non-users. Welders (76.2%), and males (89.3%) predominated in the benoxinate group ( p < 0.001). The mean duration of benoxinate use was 11.67 (2–50) days. Clinical manifestations, particularly corneal melting (15 eyes, 17.9%), eyelid contact dermatitis (9 eyes, 10.7%), ring infiltration (26 eyes, 31.0%), complications as corneal vascularization (7 eyes, 8.3%), and perforation (17 eyes, 20.2%) were significantly higher in benoxinate users. Mean difference in visual acuity before and after treatment was significantly lower in benoxinate users (0.18 ± 0.25) than in benoxinate non-users (0.34 ± 0.23), ( p < 0.001). Mean healing duration was markedly longer in benoxinate users (41.05 (4– 100)) days compared with the benoxinate non-users (7.93 (3–21)) days ( p < 0.001). Adherent leukoma was observed only in patients who continue using benoxinate after starting treatment (15 eyes, 48.4%). Conclusions Abusing topical ophthalmic anesthetics is associated with severe, permanent, and sight-threatening outcomes. Frequent and prolonged use of topical ophthalmic anesthetics aggravates ocular complications, and delays healing.

OCE: an optimization convergence metric for LiDAR SLAM degeneracy detection
abstractText: Abstract LiDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems suffer from environment-induced degeneracy in geometrically self-similar scenes such as tunnels and cylindrical structures, where the point cloud registration problem becomes ill-conditioned. Existing degeneracy detection methods predominantly rely on eigenvalue analysis of the Hessian matrix, which assesses geometric conditioning at a fixed linearization point. However, in semi-degenerate environments containing partial but sufficient geometric constraints, these methods tend to produce false positive detections because measurement noise inflates eigenvalues and obscures the contribution of minor structural features. In this paper, we propose the Optimization Convergence Efficiency (OCE) metric, which evaluates the relative contraction of the directional optimizer gradient across Levenberg-Marquardt evaluations and directly characterizes the convergence response of LiDAR registration along the monitored state direction. The proposed method is evaluated through controlled simulation with ground-truth-based quantitative assessment and real-world UAV experiments in a wind-turbine tower and a long tunnel. In the nominal simulation, OCE achieves 98.21% recall with a 2.33% false-positive rate, compared with 100% recall and a 49.42% false-positive rate for the conventional eigenvalue-ratio detector. Controlled measurement-noise experiments further demonstrate that OCE maintains substantially lower false-alarm rates as spectral discrimination becomes less reliable. These results show that OCE can retain usable LiDAR pose estimates in semi-degenerate environments while reliably identifying actual registration failure.

Lattice-Oxygen-Mediated Electronic Reconstruction of High-Entropy Oxides for Durable Fenton-like Water Treatment
abstractText: Abstract High-entropy catalysts offer broad compositional tunability for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based water treatment, yet achieving rapid, selective, and durable oxidation remains challenging because metallic bonding in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) limits electronic communication among metal sites. Here, we construct a quinary high-entropy oxide (HEO, (FeCoNiMnCu)3O4) featuring an oxygen-bridged M-O-M framework that enables local electronic coupling among neighboring metal centers. X-ray absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support oxygen-mediated charge redistribution, with Hirshfeld analysis indicating 0.46e of charge transfer toward adsorbed PMS. Temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a substantially lower apparent activation energy for interfacial charge transfer in the HEO (0.43 eV) than in the HEA (1.15 eV). Mechanistic experiments support a predominantly nonradical PMS activation pathway involving high-valent cobalt-oxo species and singlet oxygen. The HEO achieved near-complete phenol degradation and 87.9% total organic carbon removal within 10 min, with an apparent rate constant of 0.359 min–1 versus 0.113 min–1 for the HEA. The system maintained >90% phenol removal across pH 3–11, sustained activity over 30 reuse cycles, and retained effective contaminant removal during continuous-flow operation and 50 L bench-scale treatment. These results support lattice-oxygen-mediated electronic reconstruction as a strategy for coupling efficient PMS activation with structural durability in high-entropy oxide catalysts.

Enhancing Image Tampering Detection Using ResNet50 with Error Level Analysis and Gamma Correction
abstractText: Image manipulation has become increasingly sophisticated, making the verification of visual authenticity a critical challenge for preventing misinformation, fraud, and other malicious activities. Conventional detection methods often fail to capture subtle traces of tampering, motivating the use of deep learning combined with targeted preprocessing. This study proposes a detection approach that couples the ResNet50 architecture with two complementary preprocessing techniques—Error Level Analysis (ELA) and gamma correction—to sharpen the features associated with tampered regions. ELA exposes discrepancies in JPEG compression levels, while gamma correction enhances the contrast between authentic and manipulated areas; combining them yields a more discriminative feature space than either technique alone. On the CASIA 2.0 dataset (12,614 images), the model attains 82.60% accuracy without preprocessing, 95.16% with ELA, and 78.74% with gamma correction alone. Applying both techniques together produces the highest accuracy of 97.58%, a 14.98 percentage-point improvement over the baseline, because ELA isolates compression-level traces of tampering while gamma correction sharpens the contrast that makes those traces separable. These results demonstrate that carefully selected preprocessing significantly strengthens ResNet50-based image tampering detection.

title: MENAKAR KEGILAAN STRUKTURAL: DIALEKTIKA PEMIKIRAN ERICH FROMM, MICHEL FOUCAULT, DAN PETER MORRALL DALAM KRITIK MASYARAKAT MODERN
abstractText: The contemporary global mental health crisis is frequently reduced to individual biological deficits, neurological malfunctions, or neurochemical imbalances exclusively resolvable via private pharmacological interventions. This article challenges such biomedical reductions by dialectically synthesizing three macro sociological-philosophical frameworks: Erich Fromm's radical humanism in The Sane Society, Michel Foucault's archeology-genealogy of power in History of Madness, and Peter Morrall's critical sociology of mental health in Insane Society. Employing a qualitative desk-research design rooted in critical hermeneutics and comparative-conceptual analysis, literature selection was conducted using purposive sampling on primary corpuses and peer-reviewed secondary sources. The study investigates how the structural organization of modern society, dominated by late capitalism and neoliberal governance, systematically engineers existential pathologies. The findings reveal that contemporary mental distress constitutes an acute manifestation of market alienation (Fromm), a disciplinary normalization of human bodies for capitalist production (Foucault), and a systemic dysfunction of an intrinsically disordered society (Morrall). Furthermore, mainstream mental health awareness discourses operate as depoliticizing apparatuses that privatize structural suffering into personal coping failures. Resolving this crisis necessitates radical socio-political and macroeconomic structural transformations rather than privatized emotional commodification. ABSTRAK Krisis kesehatan mental global kontemporer kerap kali direduksi menjadi sekadar persoalan biologis individual, malfungsi neurologis, atau ketidakseimbangan kimiawi otak yang solusinya bertumpu pada intervensi farmakologis privat. Artikel ini menggugat simplifikasi biomedis tersebut dengan mengintegrasikan secara dialektis tiga kerangka sosiologis-filosofis makro, yakni humanisme radikal Erich Fromm melalui The Sane Society, arkeologi-genealogi kekuasaan Michel Foucault dalam History of Madness, serta sosiologi kesehatan mental kontemporer Peter Morrall lewat Insane Society. Menggunakan metode kualitatif studi kepustakaan (desk research) berbasis hermeneutika kritis dan analisis komparatif-konseptual, penentuan literatur dilakukan melalui teknik penarikan sampel bertujuan (purposive sampling) pada korpus teks primer dan sekunder bereputasi. Studi ini membedah bagaimana pola kehidupan struktural masyarakat modern, khususnya yang diatur di bawah hegemoni kapitalisme akhir dan neoliberalisme, secara inheren memproduksi patologi eksistensial. Hasil kajian menegaskan bahwa distres mental era kekinian merupakan manifestasi konkret alienasi pasar (Fromm), instrumen pendisiplinan serta normalisasi tubuh agar patuh pada mesin produksi (Foucault), dan disfungsi struktural total dari tatanan sosial yang secara sistemik sakit (Morrall). Wacana popular kesadaran kesehatan mental (mental health awareness) terbukti bertindak sebagai aparatus depolitisasi yang menundukkan penderitaan struktural menjadi kegagalan adaptasi privat. Resolusi komprehensif atas krisis mental kontemporer menuntut transformasi radikal pada struktur sosiopolitik dan ekonomi makro demi mengembalikan integritas serta otentisitas kemanusiaan.

A Fluctuating Lattice Boltzmann Model with Independent Directional Stochastic Fluctuations for Brownian Motion
abstractText: Abstract Accurate simulation of Brownian motion is essential for understanding particle dynamics at micro- and nanoscales. The fluctuating lattice Boltzmann method provides a mesoscopic framework for modeling thermal fluctuations, but conventional formulations impose identical fluctuations on opposite lattice directions, limiting independent stochastic variation. Here, we relax this symmetry by allowing independent fluctuations in each direction. Formulations are derived for the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models and applied to spherical Brownian particles, with comparisons against the conventional D3Q15 model. The simulated translational and rotational mean-square velocities are consistent with the energy equipartition theorem, confirming thermal equilibrium. The resulting diffusion coefficients demonstrate that the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models reduce the relative error by approximately 3% compared with the D3Q15 model when reproducing the Stokes-Einstein prediction. To quantify inherent errors, a correction factor α is introduced to rescale the fluctuation intensity so that the Stokes-Einstein diffusion coefficient is recovered within statistical uncertainty. The smaller α values required for the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models indicate more physically faithful stochastic behavior. The proposed methods therefore provide a more flexible and accurate representation of thermal fluctuations for Brownian motion and related microscale simulations.

title: Seasonal dynamics of heavy metal concentrations from municipal solid waste landfill leachate in Varanasi: impact on groundwater quality and human health
Next-Generation Water Quality Monitoring via Artificial Intelligence-Coupled Nanozymes
abstractText: Abstract Safe water management requires rapid and highly sensitive analytical platforms capable of detecting contaminants in complex environmental matrices. Nanozymes are nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity that offer remarkable advantages for field-deployable sensing, including stability and compatibility with portable formats. However, conventional nanozyme sensors often exhibit nonlinear catalytic behavior, limited selectivity, and susceptibility to interference in natural waters. This Perspective evaluates how integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with nanozyme-based systems can resolve these constraints. We analyze mechanistic nanozyme responses to major pollutant classes, including heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides, and show how machine learning and deep learning models enhance sensitivity, mitigate matrix effects, and enable multiplex classification via catalytic fingerprints. We further highlight emerging AI-enabled architectures, including smartphone analytics, Internet of Things (IoT)-based nanozyme devices, and cloud-connected autonomous monitoring systems. Finally, we discuss the potential of standardized datasets, digital-twin simulations, and AI-driven design of single-atom nanozymes to advance global water quality assessment.

title: PENINGKATAN HASIL BELAJAR MATEMATIKA MELALUI MODEL KOOPERATIF TIPE MAKE A MATCH PADA SISWA KELAS IV SDN DUKUH KUPANG V SURABAYA
abstractText: This classroom action research aimed to improve mathematics learning outcomes regarding division operations through the application of the "Make a Match" cooperative learning model for fourth-grade students at SDN Dukuh Kupang V Surabaya. The study employed the Kemmis and McTaggart model, comprising the stages of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. The research was conducted through a pre-action phase and two cycles, involving 28 students as research subjects. Data were collected via learning outcome tests, observations of student activity and model implementation, documentation, and reflection notes. The data were analyzed using quantitative and qualitative descriptive techniques. Learning mastery was determined using a Learning Objective Achievement Criterion (KKTP) of 75, with classical mastery targeted at a minimum of 85%. The results showed that classical learning mastery increased from 35.71% (10 of 28 students) in the pre-action phase to 67.86% (19 students) in Cycle I and 85.71% (24 students) in Cycle II. Thus, the classical mastery target was achieved in Cycle II. Furthermore, student activity increased from 70.87% in Cycle I to 87.17% in Cycle II, while implementation of the learning model improved from 75.20% to 91.00%. These findings indicate that implementing the "Make a Match" cooperative learning model through matching question and answer cards, verifying pairs, discussing, and presenting results can support learning mastery in division operations.

title: From Human Judgment to Machine Learning: A Philosophical Study of Knowledge Creation in Modern Accounting
abstractText: Background: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning into accounting and auditing has transformed the creation, validation, and application of professional knowledge, raising questions about the legitimacy of algorithmic knowledge in accounting practice. Objective: This study examines the epistemological shift from human judgment to algorithmic knowledge in the implementation of Financial Accounting Standards (Standar Akuntansi Keuangan [SAK]) and Quality Management Systems (Sistem Manajemen Mutu [SMM]). Methods: This study employs a qualitative-interpretive approach through conceptual analysis and an examination of practitioners’ perspectives on the reliability, transparency, explainability, and trustworthiness of AI-assisted decision-making. Results: The results of the study show that AI can improve efficiency, predictive accuracy, and analytical capabilities in modern accounting practices but, at the same time, poses epistemological challenges in the form of limited algorithmic transparency, limited explainability, and the potential erosion of auditors’ professional skepticism. Although the conceptual analysis indicates that AI can positively affect efficiency and predictive accuracy, it also raises epistemic challenges related to transparency, accountability, and the preservation of professional skepticism. The shift from judgment-based knowledge to data-driven inferential knowledge has transformed the traditional epistemic authority held by accountants and auditors. The application of SAK and SMM in the accounting profession has implications for defining professional responsibilities in maintaining the quality of financial reporting and audit processes. Conclusion: This study proposes a human–machine epistemic partnership, in which AI functions as an analytical augmentation tool while accountants and auditors remain the primary epistemic authorities.

title: Convxtmob-Net: A Quantum -Secure Stacked Ensemble Model for Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Prediction and Classification
abstractText: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of vision loss worldwide. With proper and timely diagnosis, vision loss can be prevented. Especially when grading is automated to improve timely decision-making by physicians. In this work, a new quantum-secure stacked ensemble approach to the DR severity classification task is proposed. To tackle the data leakage issue in clinical grading, the ConvXtMob-Net accepts out-of-the-ordinary predictions and collaboratively learns from multiple models with various topologies. Provides a Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) for secure data transmission and simulated Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for mathematically protecting proprietary model weights to tackle new security challenges in medical data transmission and edge development. ConvXtMob-Net implemented the solution and carried out a large number of experiments on the APTOS 2019 dataset, and the DDRs were 97.9% and 98.2%. Consistent Quadratic weighted kappa values of 0.97 testify to remarkable agreement in correspondence to the expert’s grading. The results indicate that the combination of stacked ensemble and post-quantum cryptography is a very precise, robust, and secure approach for automated clinical diagnostic systems.

The longhorn beetles (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) of Vitosha Mountain, Bulgaria
abstractText: Abstract The longhorn beetles (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) of Vitosha Mt. are studied based on a scientifically comprehensive review, documenting more than a century of research and original data. As a result, 134 taxa of six subfamilies have been identified: Prioninae (two species), Lepturinae (38 species and subspecies), Necydalinae (two species), Spondylidinae (seven species and subspecies), Cerambycinae (40 species and subspecies) and Lamiinae (45 species and subspecies). One of the species is new for the fauna of Bulgaria (Tetropium gabrieli Weise, 1905), while 31 of the recorded taxa are new for the fauna of Vitosha Mt. New localities within the region are reported for 73 species and subspecies, including seven rare for the country taxa. Cerambycid fauna of Vitosha Mt. is associated with deciduous trees and shrubs (59 taxa), coniferous trees and shrubs (24 taxa), deciduous and coniferous trees and shrubs (25 taxa), herbaceous plants (26 taxa) and deciduous and herbaceous plants (two taxa). Trophic associations have been established for 29 taxa of longhorn beetles with 38 tree and shrub species. The highest cerambycid diversity (116 taxa) is found in the belt of xeromesophilic and mesophilic oak-hornbeam forests (up to 1100–1400 m a.s.l.), followed by the belt of beech forests (1400–1840 m a.s.l.) where 51 cerambycid taxa have been found, the belt of coniferous forests (1700–2050 m a.s.l.) with 26 taxa, while in the belt of subalpine vegetation (above 1900 m a.s.l.) only three taxa have been recorded. The longhorn beetles belong to 19 chorological categories and eight chorological complexes. The most numerous are the taxa of the European complex (55 taxa, 41.0%), followed by those of the Palearctic complex (28 taxa, 20.9%), the Eurosiberian complex (20 taxa, 15.0%), the European-Iranoturanian complex (13 taxa, 9.7%), the Mediterranean complex (9 taxa, 6.7%), the Holarctic complex (4 taxa, 3.0%), the Balkan endemic complex (3 taxa, 2.3%) and the Cosmopolitan complex (2 taxa, 1.5%). Eighty-six species of conservation significance have been identified, which constitutes 64.2% of the total cerambycid fauna of Vitosha Mt. Two of them, Rosalia alpina and Morimus asper funereus, are protected under the Council Directive, 92/43/EEC and the Biological Diversity Act. Eighty-five species and subspecies, including Rosalia alpina, are assessed following the IUCN criteria. Among them, there are four taxa (Pedostrangalia revestita, Necydalis ulmi, Cerambyx miles, Molorchus kiesenwetteri) with a high risk of extinction (Endangered and Vulnerable categories) and four from the Near Threatened category (Rutpela septempunctata, Xylosteus bartoni, Chlorophorus herbstii and Rosalia alpina).

title: KEEFEKTIFAN KONSELING KELOMPOK KIPAS BERMUATAN BUDAYA CERITA PANJI UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KARAKTER TANGGUNG JAWAB SISWA SMK
abstractText: The low work ethic and sense of responsibility among vocational high school (SMK) students remain critical challenges directly impeding workplace readiness. Conversely, conventional guidance and counseling interventions adopting Western theories often fail to accommodate the cultural affective needs of local counselees. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of group counseling using the Intensive Progressive Adaptive Structured Counseling (KIPAS) model integrated with the cultural values of Panji Stories in improving the responsibility character of vocational students, compared to a control group receiving the Wants, Doing, Evaluation, Planning (WDEP) technique. A quantitative quasi-experimental approach was conducted using a non-equivalent control group design. The research participants comprised 18 tenth-grade students of SMKN 1 Plosoklaten selected via purposive sampling criteria exhibiting low initial responsibility scores. Data collected using a psychological responsibility scale were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test and normalized gain score (N-gain score). The findings revealed that the experimental group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement ( , ) with a final average score of 94.50, outperforming the control group which reached 88.00. Consequently, the culture-based KIPAS model is proven effective in fostering vocational students' responsibility through indigenous moral modeling. ABSTRAK Rendahnya etos kerja dan tanggung jawab siswa Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) masih menjadi persoalan krusial yang berdampak langsung pada kesiapan kerja di dunia industri. Di sisi lain, intervensi bimbingan dan konseling konvensional yang mengadopsi teori Barat sering kali kurang menyentuh ranah afeksi kultural konseli lokal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji keefektifan layanan konseling kelompok model Konseling Intensif Progresif Adaptif Struktur (KIPAS) bermuatan nilai budaya Cerita Panji dalam meningkatkan karakter tanggung jawab siswa SMK, dengan membandingkannya terhadap kelompok kontrol yang menerima teknik Wants, Doing, Evaluation, Planning (WDEP). Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui desain eksperimen semu (quasi-experimental) dengan pola non-equivalent control group design. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 18 siswa kelas X SMK Negeri 1 Plosoklaten yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan skor skala psikologis tanggung jawab kategori rendah. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji non-parametrik Mann-Whitney U dan analisis perolehan skor ternormalisasi (N-gain score). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kelompok eksperimen memperoleh peningkatan skor yang signifikan secara statistik ( , ) dengan rata-rata nilai akhir sebesar 94,50, lebih unggul dibandingkan kelompok kontrol sebesar 88,00. Dengan demikian, model konseling kelompok KIPAS bermuatan Cerita Panji terbukti efektif meningkatkan karakter tanggung jawab siswa vokasi melalui internalisasi teladan moral kearifan lokal.

AI-Based Smart Honeypot System for Cyber Attack Intelligence
abstractText: The rapid growth of digital technologies has increased the number of cyberattacks targeting online systems and user data. Traditional security methods such as firewalls and intrusion detection systems are often unable to handle advanced and evolving threats effectively. To address this issue, this paper proposes an AI-Based Smart Honeypot System for Cyberattack Intelligence that combines machine learning, behavioral analysis, and deception techniques for detecting malicious activities in real time. The proposed system monitors user activities such as login attempts, typing behavior, session timing, and interaction patterns to identify suspicious behavior. A machine learning model is used to classify users as legitimate or malicious based on these behavioral features. If suspicious activity is detected, the user is redirected to a fake environment that appears similar to a real system, allowing the collection of attacker information without exposing sensitive data. The system was tested using simulated normal and malicious user activities, and the results showed improved detection accuracy with reduced false positives. The proposed approach not only improves cybersecurity protection but also helps in gathering valuable cyber threat intelligence for future analysis. Overall, the system provides a practical and scalable solution for modern cybersecurity challenges.
